title: PRD: Multi-modal Hosted Endpoint — Compatibility, Opt-in Policies & Progressive Launch Playbook
creator: Sofia Patel
description: This ticket captures the product requirements and launch readiness checklist for a single, multi-modal hosted endpoint that supports chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank modalities via a unified contract. The goal is to define compatibility rules, opt-in behavior for new features (structured output, function-calling, streaming), acceptance criteria across modalities, and a progressive rollout plan that minimizes customer regressions and operational risk.
background: Customers ask for a single, consistent endpoint and SDK experience while we continue to offer specialized behavioral guarantees for each modality. Previous PRDs split endpoints by capability and led to duplicated maintenance and developer confusion. This PRD proposes a consolidated surface with clear modality flags, backward compatible defaults, and a staged launch to validate quality and infra stability.
goals: Deliver a single hosted endpoint API that can serve chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank requests with explicit modality routing.
Preserve backward compatibility for existing hosted consumers; all current endpoints continue to behave identically unless the customer opts into new capability flags.
Provide deterministic acceptance criteria for each modality (latency SLOs, token-cost estimates, quality guardrails, and fallback behavior).
Define an operational progressive rollout with telemetry gates and rollback actions to protect SLAs.
non_goals: This ticket does not include migrating Dedicated or Private control planes — those will be tracked in separate infra migration tasks.
We will not change existing billing models or token accounting in this launch; pricing changes are a follow-up where necessary.
We are not adding new model architectures (e.g., multimodal image input) in this launch — text-only modalities only.
scope: API surface: single endpoint /v1/hosted-call that includes a required 'modality' field (chat|completion|embedding|rerank).
SDK: client helper wrappers in official JS/Python SDKs to map legacy calls to the unified endpoint.
Server-side: routing layer that selects model variants and execution parameters per modality and policy-based fallbacks.
Telemetry: modality-specific metrics (p50/p95 latency, tokens per request, quality regressions via eval harness), and release flags in Console.
Acceptance tests: automated integration tests per modality and chaos tests for fallback paths.
technical_requirements: Request contract includes: modality, model_version (optional), streamed=true|false, function_calling=opt_in flag, structured_output=opt_in flag.
Runtime must offer per-modality kernel selection and batching policies. Default batching profiles must be validated against p95 latency targets defined in acceptance criteria.
KV cache behavior: preserved for chat modality; explicitly disabled for embeddings and rerank to avoid contamination of vector caches.
Fallbacks: policy to degrade from high-cost model to cheaper variant within same family when capacity constrained; must be observable and reversible.
Rollout toggle: per-customer and global feature flags in Console with audit logs.
ux_requirements: Console: new 'Endpoint' creation flow with modality selector and pre-populated acceptance profiles.
SDK ergonomics: mapping helpers to translate legacy 'chat.create' and 'completions.create' to unified call with minimal code changes.
Errors: clear error codes for modality mismatch, deprecated model, or missing opt-in flags with suggested remediation text.
acceptance_criteria: Functional: For each modality the unified endpoint returns identical outputs to legacy endpoints when called with backward-compatible flags (sanity harness against canonical test corpus).

Latency: p50/p95 for chat and completions must be within 10% of legacy endpoint baselines measured across representative traffic; embeddings and rerank p95 must meet defined targets (embeddings p95 <= 120ms on hosted-prod baseline).
Quality: end-to-end behavioral regression tests (automated eval suite) show no more than 1% drop in aggregated quality score vs legacy endpoints for top-10 prompts per workload.
Observability: modality-specific dashboards in Console exist and show real traffic within 24 hours of rollout; logs include model_version and fallback events.
Safety & Security: opt-in structured output and function-calling only enabled after security review; audit logs capture opt-ins and schema versions.
Migration: SDK adapters provided with migration guide and automated compatibility tests; documented deprecation schedule for legacy endpoints.
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal Redwood services + 3 friendly customers (opt-in) for 2 weeks to validate functional parity and quality signals.
Beta: open to existing customers by invite with feature flag per-customer; monitor for 4 weeks and require no critical regressions before wider rollout.
Canary: 5% of overall hosted traffic with automatic rollback on infra or quality gate violations for 72 hours.
GA: full launch after successful canary and postmortem; enable migration docs and deprecation notices for legacy endpoints.
launch_checklist: PRD sign-off from Product, Eng, and Design.
Security review completed and approval stored in Console audit folder.
SDK releases (JS, Python) with automated compatibility tests and migration guide published.
Console: rollout toggles implemented and verified in staging; endpoint creation UX validated by UX research.
Telemetry: modality dashboards, alerts, and anomaly detectors configured and smoke-tested.
Runbooks: incident runbook and rollback playbook published and distributed to on-call rotation.
Legal/compliance: updated terms if needed and documentation for customers on opt-in behavioral features.
Performance: baseline load tests and p95 latency verified under 2x expected peak load with conservative autoscaling settings.
milestones: 2026-03-08: API contract finalized and PRD approved by stakeholders.
2026-04-12: Canary completion and GA readiness decision.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Quality regressions for edge-case prompts when moving to unified routing. Mitigation: maintain legacy model routing as fallback and run targeted evals during alpha.
Risk: Unexpected cost increases due to batching changes. Mitigation: conservative batching profiles and cost telemetry; temporary hard limits during canary.
Risk: Customer confusion migrating SDK calls. Mitigation: provide migration script, automated compatibility tests, and proactive outreach to top-50 customers.
open_questions: Should we expose modality as a top-level URL path (/v1/hosted/chat vs /v1/hosted-call + modality)? Pros/cons for routing observability.
What is the minimum viable structured_output schema version we can ship without blocking security review?
Do we require explicit opt-in for function-calling for all customers or only for GA customers with contract addendum?
